entries.title: How Gemini Flash agents are helping a Michigan dairy farmer
entries.summary: Using Gemini to manage a farm
entries.content:
Dairy farming operates on tight margins, making data analysis essential for managing complex biological and environmental variables. Since modern farms generate massive volumes of information, the challenge lies in analyzing it quickly to make decisions. That’s why Paul Windemuller turned to Gemini 3.6 Flash.

In 2014, Paul and Brittany started Dream Winds Dairy in Michigan with 30 leased cows. Over 12 years, it grew into a highly automated facility milking 260 Holsteins. As a 2024 Nuffield International Farming Scholar studying ag tech and AI, Paul approaches dairy farming as a technological challenge.

His operations generate continuous data streams: sensor collars track each cow, a local weather station records climate metrics, and an online portal logs milk quality and shipments.

However, these systems operate in isolated software silos. Every morning, Paul spent hours downloading files, merging spreadsheets, and calculating performance. This kept him away from actually looking after the cows.

Delegating the office work to AI agents

To reclaim his time, Paul built a local, multi-agent AI system using Gemini 3.6 Flash inside Google Antigravity to integrate siloed farm data and calculate daily profitability.

Instead of APIs or web scraping, the system uses a local, directory-based file-interface. When CSV data exports or photos of papers receipts, PDFs, and invoices are saved to a monitored folder, Gemini’s multimodal power extracts and merges visual and numeric metrics — keeping data under Paul’s control.

A specialized multi-agent workflow replaces long prompts with specialized, orchestrated roles:

  • Orchestrator: Manages the overall daily workflow.
  • Ingestion Agents: Standardize raw files (milking robot exports, feed logs).
  • Analysis Agent: Evaluates biological and weather impacts.
  • Reporting Agent: Generates clear, natural language summaries.

The system automatically transforms raw files into a cohesive business overview.

Leveling the playing field for small businesses

Ultimately, Paul’s ambition is to empower independent farmers with technology they can use to streamline their operations the same way he has been able to for his own business. Not only is building the tool a hurdle for many, but once they have them, operating at farm scale was a cost challenge that needed to be solved.

The daily agentic workflows that require continuous reasoning, parsing, and tool execution have been too expensive for small businesses like his. Gemini 3.6 Flash helped make Paul's daily operation more cost-effective.

Designed for advanced reasoning, tool use, and coding, Gemini 3.6 Flash features a 1 million token context window and a 64,000 token maximum output. Benchmark evaluations show it achieves roughly a 17 percent reduction in output tokens compared to Gemini 3.5 Flash, at a lower cost per output token, significantly lowering the cost of running agentic loops.

Measuring success by Static Variable Margin

The system is designed to optimize for Paul’s primary metric: Daily Static Variable Margin (SVM). Unlike traditional metrics like Income Over Feed Cost, which fluctuates with volatile milk and feed prices, SVM holds market prices constant, isolating the true biological and operational efficiency from market noise. This grounds the agentic system in a truth Paul can rely on to give him actionable insights for farm operations.

How the agentic workflow calculates SVM

  • Biological Performance: Ingestion agents parse milk yields, components (butterfat/protein), somatic cell count, and feed.
  • Static Revenue: Applies fixed prices based on historical pay standards ( Federal Order 33 January prices) to actual milk solids produced.
  • Static Feed Cost: Uses fixed ingredient prices to isolate changes in actual feed volume consumed.
  • Static Income Over Feed Cost: Subtracts the static feed cost from static revenue.
  • Variable Costs: Subtracts per-cow expenses (replacements, breeding, vet supplies) while excluding overhead (labor, utilities, depreciation), ensuring SVM changes reflect only biological efficiency and health.

Generating the Daily Briefing

Calculating numbers is only half the battle. Busy farmers don’t have time to decode spreadsheets every morning at 3:00 AM. To save time, the reporting agent translates results into a daily Farm CEO Briefing that isolates daily margin drivers. For example, if SVM drops by $0.15 per cow, it pinpoints specific causes:

  • Dry Matter Intake: -$0.08 ( humidity reduced feed intake)
  • Somatic Cell Count: -$0.04 (slight increase indicating potential health issues)
  • Discarded Milk: -$0.03 (two cows entered the treatment pen)

It ends with actionable recommendations, such as adjusting ventilation for heat stress. Since the system runs on local file exports, all sensitive data stays on the farm.

Scaling independent businesses beyond the spreadsheet

Paul’s agentic system built in Antigravity highlights a major shift for small businesses, which he hopes can inspire and teach others how they may evaluate using AI in their daily workflows. By pairing multi-agent architecture with the low cost token efficiency of Gemini 3.6 Flash, he built an automated operating layer that eliminates hours of manual spreadsheet work, allowing him to step out of the office, and focus on growing his business.

entries.title: Gemini API Managed Agents: 3.6 Flash, hooks, and more
entries.summary: Managed Agents Gemini 3.6 Flash, Hooks and Triggers
entries.content:
Managed Agents in Gemini API are getting environment hooks, model selection, and free tier access. These capabilities build on our previous release introducing background tasks and remote MCP server integration.

With managed agents in the Gemini Interactions API, a single API call coordinates, reasoning, code execution, package installation, file management, and web retrieval inside an isolated cloud sandbox.

If you're using an AI coding assistant, drop this in your terminal to give it access to the Interactions API skill: 

npx skills add google-gemini/gemini-skills --skill gemini-interactions-api.

Below are examples using the 

@google/genai
TypeScript/JavaScript SDK. For Python or cURL, check out the Antigravity agent documentation.
npm install @google/genai

Gemini 3.6 Flash is now the default

The 

antigravity-preview-05-2026
agent now runs Gemini 3.6 Flash by default. No code changes are required. Your next interaction picks it up automatically.

You can also explicitly select models by passing 

agent_config.model
when creating an interaction or managed agent. Use Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite for lower cost, or pin to your model of preference.
import { GoogleGenAI } from "@google/genai";

const client = new GoogleGenAI({});

const interaction = await client.interactions.create({
  agent: "antigravity-preview-05-2026",
  input: "Audit all dependencies in package.json, upgrade outdated packages, and verify the build by running npm test.",
  environment: "remote",
  agent_config: {
    type: "antigravity",
    model: "gemini-3.5-flash-lite",
  },
});

console.log(interaction.output_text);

Supported models include:

  • Gemini 3.6 Flash (
    gemini-3.6-flash
    , default): Balanced model for reasoning, coding, and tool use.
  • Gemini 3.5 Flash (
    gemini-3.5-flash
    ): Previous generation for general agentic workflows.
  • Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite (
    gemini-3.5-flash-lite
    ): Lowest latency and cost on the Gemini 3.5 family.

Environment hooks: block, lint, and audit tool calls inside the sandbox

Environment hooks let you run your custom scripts before or after every tool call the agent makes inside its sandbox. Add a .

agents/hooks.json
into your environment and the runtime executes your handlers on 
pre_tool_execution or post_tool_execution
events.

The 

matcher
field supports regular expressions, allowing you to target multiple tools with 
|
or catch everything with 
*
:
{
  "security-gate": {
    "pre_tool_execution": [
      {
        "matcher": "code_execution|write_file",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 /.agents/hooks-scripts/gate.py",
            "timeout": 10
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "auto-format": {
    "post_tool_execution": [
      {
        "matcher": "*",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "python3 /.agents/hooks-scripts/auto_lint.py",
            "timeout": 15
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}

In this configuration:

  • The 
    security-gate
    group runs
    gate.py
    before every
    code_execution
    or
    write_file
    call. If the script returns
    {"decision": "deny", "reason": "..."}
    , the tool call is skipped and the rejection reason is passed into the model’s context.
  • The 
    auto-format
    group runs
    auto_lint.py
    after every tool finishes to enforce code styling.
  • Hooks also support 
    http
    type handlers that POST directly to an external endpoint.

For complete HTTP hook definitions and failure handling semantics, refer to the hooks documentation.

Teams are already using hooks to build production-grade validation pipelines. For example, AI-native investment bank Offdeal uses 

post_tool_execution
hooks to run automated image verification inside the remote sandbox.

"OffDeal is an AI-native investment bank, and Archie is the AI analyst our bankers use every day. A requirement for banker-ready decks is company logos: buyer tables, sponsor columns, tombstone grids, often 30+ logos in a single deck, every one of which must be the right company, the appropriate size and aspect ratio, contain the name, have a transparent background, and have a high contrast when placed on a white slide.

Before agent hooks, we couldn’t do this on Gemini’s managed agents: the sandbox is remote, so our validation code had nowhere to run. With hooks, a post_tool_execution hook triggers our pipeline inside the sandbox the moment Archie writes its company list, fetching candidates, enforcing pixel-level quality checks, verifying each logo with Gemini vision, and publishing a manifest of approved files that are the only images allowed into the deck."

- Alston Lin, Founder & CTO of OffDeal

Cost control and automation features

Free tier availability

Managed agents are now available on free tier projects. Developers can experiment with agentic workflows using an API key from a project without active billing.

Budget controls

Because managed agents execute multi-turn autonomous loops, complex tasks can consume significant token budgets. To prevent runaway tasks, you can pass 

max_total_tokens
inside 
agent_config
to cap total consumption (input + output + thinking).

When the agent reaches the limit, execution safely pauses and the interaction returns 

status: "incomplete"
. The environment state is preserved, enabling you to continue where it stopped by passing 
previous_interaction_id
with a fresh budget.
const interaction = await client.interactions.create({
  agent: "antigravity-preview-05-2026",
  input: "Audit all modules in this repo and generate a migration report.",
  agent_config: {
    type: "antigravity",
    max_total_tokens: 10000,
  },
  environment: "remote",
});

Scheduled execution with triggers

Automate recurring agent tasks with scheduled triggers. A trigger binds an agent, environment, prompt, and cron schedule into a persistent resource that fires without manual intervention. Each run reuses the same sandbox, so files persist across executions.

Environments API

The Environments API lets you list, inspect, and delete sandbox sessions from code. Recover environment IDs after a disconnect, or clean up sandboxes when your pipeline finishes instead of waiting for the 7-day TTL.

Get started with managed agents

These updates turn managed agents into cost-controlled, scheduled workers that operate autonomously inside real development environments without breaking your budget or requiring external orchestration.

Check out the Gemini Interactions API overview and the managed agents quickstart to explore custom agent definitions, environment configurations, network rules, and advanced streaming patterns.

entries.title: 3 new ways nonprofits can put AI to work
entries.summary: A man points to a computer screen. Another man smiles looking at the screen.
entries.content:
In the rugged fjords of New Zealand, the volunteer-led Tawaki Project once spent six weeks manually transcribing handwritten research data on penguins. But after adopting Google for Nonprofits, they turned a 240-hour task into mere minutes.

The team used Google Sheets and Maps Platform API credits to build an interactive tracking platform. This rapid data processing and visualization helped the team secure $1.1 million in funding and contribute to reclassifying the Fiordland crested penguin from "vulnerable" to "near threatened."

The Tawaki Project saw a boost in efficiency from our Google for Nonprofits program, and they’re not alone. On average, nonprofit participants report saving one full workday per person, per week on administrative tasks with AI.

To help more organizations put AI to work for their missions, we’re introducing new tools and resources for nonprofits on google.com/nonprofits:

  • Practical, on-demand training: We are launching three free of charge, nonprofit-specific online courses to help teams use AI effectively. The courses focus on the topics nonprofits told us they believe could have transformative potential to improve with AI: fundraising, marketing, and operations. In around three hours, participants can learn practical skills from Daily wins with AI,Optimize Creativity and Fundraising, andBuild Smarter Workflows.
  • One-on-one productivity coaching: We're offering all Google for Nonprofits organizations personalized, hands-on support and training from Google Product Specialists at no cost. After activating Google Workspace for Nonprofits, your team can schedule 1:1 video chat sessions to get expert guidance on everything from technical migration to training staff on the latest AI tools.
  • Key insights: 86% of surveyed nonprofits agree that AI has the potential to make their personal work more effective, yet organizations report that, on average, less than half (49%) of their organization uses AI regularly. Nonprofits tell us funding and access to training are the top bottlenecks to adoption. To maximize peer learning, we’re publishing the results of how over 6,000 Google for Nonprofits organizations are integrating AI into their daily operations, the barriers they face, and recommendations to help all nonprofits make use of AI for the greatest impact.

Today’s announcement furthers our mission to help nonprofits experience the opportunities created by technology — expanding on the $18+ billion in free-of-charge technology we’ve provided so far. Read the full insights here and explore the new training and coaching options at google.com/nonprofits.

entries.title: 5 ways AI Mode in Search helps you enjoy the real world
entries.summary: Illustration of a black magnifying glass in a white circle on green grass surrounded by items related to fun activities like tennis and games
entries.content:
People are searching for more and more ways to get offline, experience the real world, and “touch grass.” This year, people are searching for “adult tennis lessons,” “trail running,” “hiking,” and “run club” more than ever before. People are also searching for questions like “how to digital detox” (+110% since the beginning of the year) and “how to meet people my age near me.”

To make the most of your IRL fun, AI Mode in Google Search has the tools to help you find the information you need. Here's how:

1. Find local classes that fit into your schedule.

Ready to try your hand at something new but don’t know where to begin? Use AI Mode to kick things off by asking something like, "How can I get started playing tennis? Are there beginner clinics or lessons nearby that I could easily join?"

Personal Intelligence allows you to securely connect the dots across your Google apps so that AI Mode’s responses are even more personalized to you. For example, say you’re looking to get better at cooking and want to find classes that’d easily fit into your schedule next month. If you’ve chosen to connect Google Calendar, you’ll get suggestions that fit your existing schedule.

2. Find the exact gear you need.

Getting outdoors is a great way to disconnect, but for activities like hiking and trail running, you want to make sure you’re fully prepared before you head out. You can easily shop within AI Mode to make sure you have the items to exactly fit your needs. Try asking, "Can you help me find some affordable hiking boots with good ankle support?" AI Mode will help you choose between products that match what you’re looking for. You can also see what’s in stock in the area by including “nearby” or “near me” in your search, and even ask Google to call nearby stores to get product availability for you.

3. Perfect your strategy.

If you’re getting into tabletop games this year, you can use Canvas in AI Mode to create a guide to help you memorize some of the core playing strategies. Head to AI Mode, tap the plus menu, select Canvas, then ask it something like, “I know the basics of playing chess and what the different pieces do, but I want to up my game. Make a guide with a few easy to remember strategies I can start using immediately to get an edge when I play my friends.” Once you’ve mastered key moves, you can even use Canvas to practice by building a game simulation where you play against a computer.

4. Find and book event tickets.

If you like spending your time offline by attending live events, use AI Mode to help you find and book tickets for nearby events, like concerts and sports. Share details like your budget, how many tickets you want, and what event you’d like to go to. AI Mode will curate a list of options, so you can finalize your booking at your preferred platform to secure your spot.

5. Design a dinner party invite.

Hosting a dinner party is a great way to put your phone away and spend quality time with friends. By connecting some of your go-to apps, like Canva, to Search, you can easily turn any inspiration into an editable design all in one space. Simply try a prompt like, "Create a flyer in Canva for the party I’m hosting in two weeks. Make it modern minimalistic style." Canva will generate a custom design right in your Search results. You can add finishing design touches in Canva, or easily download it, and send it out. Then you can get back to planning your tablescape design.

Need some more inspiration? Dive deeper into what people are searching for as they look to unplug intentionally.

entries.title: These Google Trends show people really want to touch grass
entries.summary: Illustration of a phone in do-not-disturb mode against green grass
entries.content:
This year, it seems like everyone is looking for ways to unplug, go offline, and connect with others. Searches for “how to digital detox” are up +110% since the beginning of this year, and “how to touch grass” is a breakout search over the past month.

If you don’t know what touching grass means, you’re not alone — searches for “meaning of touch grass” are up 90% this year. To put it simply, touching grass means intentionally taking time to reconnect with the physical world. Our latest Google Trends deep-dive into search behavior shows that people are increasingly seeking out more in-person connection, more time spent outdoors, and more opportunities to learn. Here’s a look at the trending hobbies and activities people are exploring this year.

Logging off and lacing up

Searches show that people are eager to get moving together. “Run club” and “how to start running” hit all-time high search interest in 2026, with “how to find local run clubs” and “how to make friends at run club” as related breakout questions in the past month.

But running isn’t the only organized outdoor activity people are looking for. Searches for “walking club” reached a 10-year high in 2026, and people are searching for “adult tennis lessons” and “hiking” more than ever this year.

Getting competitive and crafty

Tabletop games and crafts are also capturing people’s interest. Searches for “mahjong for beginners” increased by +230% over the past year, and "mahjong lessons near me" have doubled since the start of 2026. We also saw search interest in “chess classes near me” double over the past month, with “chess tactics for beginners” as a trending search in the same timeframe.

Classic hobbies are making a comeback. Knitting, crocheting, needlepoint and more, affectionately called "grandma hobbies”are on the rise. “How to start a cross stitch pattern” and “is knitting or crochet easier” are also breakout searches in the past month, while needlepoint is the top trending beginner craft kit. Search interest in “how to make my own” reached an all-time high this year, and “how to make my own embroidery designs” is a breakout related search in the past month. And many people want to quite literally touch some greenery, with “floral arranging classes near me” searches up 850% in the past month.

Gathering around the table

While it’s fun to get out and socialize, searches show that people are looking for ways to bring the party home, too. “How to host a cocktail party” and “how to host a garden party” are trending searches in the past month, while “mahjong dinner party” is a breakout dinner party theme.

From hosting the best dinner party to finding the best beginner hiking shoes, Google Search can help you find the information you need to make the most of your time offline.

entries.title: 5 ways to host the ultimate dinner party with Google Search
entries.summary: An illustrated black magnifying glass with a sparkle in a white circle surrounded by a dinner party tablescape
entries.content:
Planning the perfect dinner party is an art. Even if you love to host, it can be stressful to navigate logistics like crafting menus and designing tablescapes. Luckily, Search can help.

As more people are looking to find ways to connect in real life, dinner party-related queries are also trending. People are turning to Search for inspiration, assistance with nitty-gritty planning, and more:

  • “what is a progressive dinner party,” “how to set table for dinner party,” and “what to wear to a dinner party” were some of the top trending questions about “dinner party” this year so far.
  • “mahjong dinner party” was a breakout dinner party theme over the past month.
  • “how to keep pasta warm for dinner party” and “elegant chicken recipes for dinner party” were breakout “for dinner party” searches over the past month.
  • “how to host a cocktail party” and “how to host a garden party” were top trending “how to host” searches over the past month.

With Google’s latest AI Search tools, you have even more ways to bring your dinner parties to the next level. Here are some of the top ways Search can make you the host with the most.

1. Visualize a creative tablescape with Nano Banana.

Half the fun of hosting is coming up with beautiful and thematic tablescapes and decorations to set the stage for the meal. If you need a few suggestions on how to transform your space, you can turn to Nano Banana in AI Mode in Search to visualize how your table could look.

2. Discover the perfect menu.

The meal is at the center of every dinner party. But building a unique menu that will surprise and delight your guests can be as tricky as pulling off the perfect soufflé. You can use AI Mode to help you come up with food themes or brainstorm menu options that match your party’s vibe. And now, you can try our new visual treatment in AI Mode that makes it easier to discover dishes from recipe creators. When you search for a recipe, prominent links will appear at the top of responses with images and useful details like the creator’s name, recipe ratings, and number of ingredients.

3. Have AI Mode recommend drink pairings for your menu.

Once you’ve landed on your dishes, you can turn to AI Mode to recommend drinks. For example, if you ask AI Mode, “I need help with drink pairings for my dinner party. What should I buy that goes with miso salmon? I'll also serve a cheese platter and key lime pie,” you’ll get several recommendations for what you should purchase and why it complements your meal.

4. Connect your go-to apps to create playlists and more.

Now that you can connect some of your go-to apps directly to Search, there are even more ways to make your dinner party shine. For example, you can use AI Mode to curate a playlist that matches your vibe, instantly save it to YouTube Music and press play to start setting the tone for your party.

5. Design a menu that reflects your style.

A well-designed menu can bring the whole dinner party together. With Nano Banana in AI Mode, you can also design a menu to print or share in seconds. Try asking, “I'm doing a caprese salad appetizer followed by chicken piccata as the main course and tiramisu for dessert. Could you visualize a menu that I can print and put on the table?”

From creating a menu to discovering the perfect dish to serve, let Search do your dinner party heavy lifting so you can focus on enjoying the company of your guests.

entries.title: Google and KDDI are ready to back Japanese startups.
entries.summary: We’re launching the AI Startup Support Program to accelerate innovative AI-native Japanese startups.
entries.content:
The Google AI Futures Fund backs the startups that are building what’s next in AI — and we’re extending our support to Japan. In partnership with Japanese telecom leader KDDI, we’re launching the AI Startup Support Program to accelerate the most innovative AI-native Japanese startups. This initiative is built on our conviction that Japan is home to some of the most visionary AI builders in the world.

Selected startups will receive:

  • Joint funding: Equity investments from both the AI Futures Fund and KDDI Open Innovation Fund.
  • The latest AI models: Early access to some of Google’s most advanced AI tools — including Gemini, Nano Banana, and Lyria — plus, opportunities to provide feedback to the researchers building them.
  • Compute credits: Google Cloud credits, as well as credits for sovereign Gemini and GPUs, uniquely provisioned in Japan via KDDI’s Osaka-Sakai Data Center.
  • Dedicated support: Hands-on technical support from a network of Google and KDDI researchers, engineers, product managers, and more, as well as distribution and business opportunities.

Learn more about the program on the AI Futures Fund website. We encourage any Japanese team with an ambitious vision to apply.

entries.title: NOAA and Google Cloud collaborate to advance weather forecasting.
entries.summary: Google Cloud is now providing high-performance computing infrastructure for NOAA’s supercomputing system.
entries.content:
Accurate weather forecasting saves lives and protects infrastructure, but predicting complex global atmospheric patterns requires immense computing power. NOAA (National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration) is taking a major leap forward by selecting Google Cloud as the primary provider of high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure for its Weather and Climate Operational Supercomputing System (WCOSS).

By transitioning to Google Cloud’s H4D virtual machines, NOAA becomes one of the first major global weather centers to move operational numerical weather prediction directly to the public cloud. This migration gives meteorologists and researchers unprecedented scale, speed, and AI capabilities to run massive simulations, refine prediction models, and issue faster, life-saving early warnings.

Read more on the Google Cloud blog.

entries.title: Google is signing the EU AI Act Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content.
entries.content:
We’re signing the EU AI Act Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content to help support the responsible use of AI in Europe. This builds on our 2025 signing of the GPAI Code of Practice and aligns with our ongoing work to adopt and accelerate the C2PA industry standard and to develop AI transparency tools — including SynthID. SynthID is our industry-leading digital watermarking technology that helps people understand how content was created and edited. To promote trust across platforms, we have also been partnering with third-party AI labs like Apple, Eleven Labs, Kakao, NVIDIA, and OpenAI to drive industry-wide adoption of interoperable watermarking tools using SynthID.

While we support transparency, we are concerned that adding more regulatory complexity — as technical solutions are still evolving — could contradict Europe’s goals for competitiveness and simplification. It also risks confusing the people these rules are meant to help. If online content is flooded with overlapping AI labels and legal disclosures, it becomes harder for people to get the clear context they need.

As this code is implemented, we will work together with regulators and partners to build practical solutions that provide real transparency and help people make informed decisions about the content they see online.
